ARABIC — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.

2. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.

3. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

4. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.

5. When practising Reading Aloud: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Fluency.

6. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

7. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.

8. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

9. When practising Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Imitative Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Conversational Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud: Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud: Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading aloud: Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
